package_info.package_versions: ctx: 0.1.2 and other recent versions after 8 years of inactivity; PHPass: 0.3.x-dev (recent commit)
package_info.why_malicious: Both packages were hijacked and modified to exfiltrate sensitive environment variables, including AWS credentials, to an external endpoint controlled by the attacker. This constitutes credential theft and supply chain compromise, far exceeding any legitimate PoC or bug bounty demonstration.

execution_context.trigger: import-time / runtime (whenever PasswordHash class is instantiated)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Reads AWS credentials from environment variables and exfiltrates them via an HTTP GET request to a remote Heroku endpoint.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code steals sensitive credentials and sends them to an external server, which is a classic credential exfiltration technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A password hashing library should never access environment variables for AWS credentials or make unsolicited network requests.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate code might read environment variables for configuration, but never to exfiltrate secrets to a third-party endpoint.
key_indicators: Accessing AWS credentials in a password hashing class
Unsolicited HTTP request to a non-affiliated domain
Use of environment variables for credential theft

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Import-time exfiltration of environment variables is a hallmark of supply chain attacks. The code is not part of any legitimate library functionality.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A context management library should not access or transmit environment variables, especially secrets, to external servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate telemetry might send anonymized usage data, but never secrets or credentials.
key_indicators: Accessing and exfiltrating all environment variables

behavioral_signatures: Import-time or constructor-time network requests to untrusted domains
Access to environment variables unrelated to package functionality
Exfiltration of AWS or other cloud credentials
file_indicators: References to external endpoints (e.g., herokuapp.com) in source code
New author or maintainer metadata in package files
network_indicators: Unusual outbound traffic during package import or installation
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for packages that access environment variables and make network requests at import or constructor time. Flag any code that sends environment variables or credentials to external, non-affiliated domains. Use static analysis to detect hardcoded URLs and dynamic analysis to observe runtime exfiltration behavior. Monitor for unexpected changes in package metadata, such as new authors or maintainers.
